meta.what: The project's reading convention, under the ruling recorded as proposal 8 in docs/decisions-log.md.
meta.credit: The pronunciations are Thuum.org's, from its Fifth Edition dictionary (non-commercial use; see research/sources/thuum/ATTRIBUTION.md). The dictionary calls them recommended, not official.
ruling: The Fifth Edition's per-word pronunciations are the reading convention.
Where its table and its entries disagree, the entries are followed.
Where an entry lists several pronunciations, the first is taught and the rest are accepted.
Stress is taught as marked and described as a tendency.
It is labelled everywhere as a convention, not official.
For new words the pronunciation is worked out from the spelling by the rule below.

Owner's condition: people will at some point listen to the game. The convention stays open to that evidence. What is heard in the game is recorded per word under heard_in_game, with the speaker and line; a form heard in the game is accepted, and where the game consistently contradicts the taught form, the taught form changes in a numbered release.
meta.notation: International Phonetic Alphabet. A space separates syllables; ˈ marks primary stress and ˌ secondary stress on the syllable that follows.

rule_for_new_words.method: Each spelling unit takes the sound the dictionary most often gives it, separately for a stressed syllable (S), an unstressed one (U), an unstressed one at the end of the word (Ufinal) and for consonants (C).
rule_for_new_words.stress_finding: Stress cannot be worked out from spelling alone: the best simple rule matches about two words in three. The dictionary ties stress to the root of a word, which spelling does not show. In the forge the coiner declares the parts of a new word, so stress is placed on the root; for a new root the default is the first syllable.

how_well_it_reproduces_the_dictionary.test: five-fold cross-validation over 644 entries: the rule is learned from four fifths and tried on the rest
how_well_it_reproduces_the_dictionary.note: A match means every sound is the same as in the dictionary's pronunciation; stress marks and syllable breaks are not compared.
